checks.title: New mail reaches every open mail client, in rising UIDs, including mail that finishes arriving late and mail behind a bad message
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: New mail reaches every open mail client
  Given a Mac mail client idling on INBOX and an iPhone mail client with INBOX selected
  And the mailbox already holds messages the clients have been told about
  When mail arrives in this order: a large message whose receipt began before a small one but finished storing after the small one was shown, a message whose stored copy is missing, a message that cannot be read, a message with no Message-ID, and an ordinary message
  And the iPhone selects INBOX again
  Then the Mac is told of each new message without sending a command
  And the iPhone and the Mac see every new message under the same UID
  And every new UID is greater than every UID either client was told before
  And the late large message, the message with no Message-ID and the ordinary message all appear
  And the missing and unreadable messages appear as no message and hold back none after them
proves: FR-MAIL-034: keep each mailbox in one Durable Object that pulls deliveries into SQLite
FR-MAIL-034: assigning UIDs that only rise
FR-MAIL-034: never losing a delivery that commits late (form 01a19daa saw a cursor at the newest id lose mail for good)
FR-MAIL-034: never letting one bad message stop later ones
FR-MAIL-034: tell every registered IMAP session of any change (form 01a19daa: a row pulled by one client's SELECT must still tell the client in IDLE)
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Two mail clients see it through IMAP over several deliveries and commands, so it is a sequence through a public surface.

checks.title: A message one client expunges stays readable to the other until it is told, and never comes back or gives up its UID
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: One client expunges a message another client is looking at
  Given a Mac and an iPhone mail client with INBOX selected, both told of the newest message
  When the Mac flags the second message as seen
  And the Mac deletes and expunges the newest message
  Then the iPhone is told the second message's new flags and the expunge
  And before it is told, the iPhone can still fetch the expunged message's body in full
  When the provider delivers the expunged message again with the same Message-ID
  And a new message arrives
  And a third client selects INBOX
  Then the third client does not see the expunged message
  And the redelivered copy adds no message
  And the new message's UID is greater than the expunged message's UID
proves: FR-MAIL-034: keeping an expunged message's bytes readable until they are erased
FR-MAIL-034: keeping an expunged message's row (no UID reused, a redelivery adds no message)
FR-MAIL-034: assigning UIDs that only rise (an expunged highest UID is not reused)
FR-MAIL-034: tell every registered IMAP session of any change (flags and expunge)
toy 01a19d7e: the mailbox never reuses a UID and gives a held Message-ID no UID
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Three clients meet it through IMAP across flag, expunge, redelivery and select, so it takes many calls through a public surface.

checks.title: A client's own command that brings in or changes mail is answered
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A client's own command that brings in or changes mail is answered
  Given a Mac mail client idling on INBOX and an iPhone mail client logged in
  And new mail has arrived that neither client has been told about
  When the iPhone selects INBOX
  Then the iPhone's SELECT is answered and lists the new mail
  When the iPhone flags a message and then expunges another
  Then each command is answered
  And the Mac is told of the new mail, the flag and the expunge
  And mail arriving afterwards still reaches both clients
proves: FR-MAIL-034: without ever waiting for the telling
form 01a19daa (seen failure): a tell waiting on the session whose own SELECT caused the pull hung the mailbox and every ping for good
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The hang shows only as an IMAP command that never answers, across a sequence of client commands, so a client would notice it.

checks.title: A pull adds every delivery exactly once, however late or crowded it commits within the lag
checks.rule: pull() adds every delivery that commits within ten minutes of its id exactly once, with a cursor ten minutes behind the newest id seen, dashed like the ids, that only rises, paging by the last id read, single-flight with one more pass, and each row's insert or skip committed with the cursor in one transaction; rows: a delivery 5 s ahead of the cursor; a delivery committing behind the newest id; a row read behind the cursor leaves it unlowered; 101 deliveries inside the lag window; two overlapping pulls of a message with no Message-ID; a ping during a pull; a pull failing between a row's insert and the cursor.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: never losing a delivery that commits late
FR-MAIL-034: assigning UIDs that only rise (no delivery added twice)
form 01a19daa (seen failure): a delivery cursor at the newest id lost mail for good
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Boundary ids, overlapping pulls and a failure between two writes cannot be arranged through an IMAP client, so the scenario cannot show these rows failing.

checks.title: No committed change stays untold, and no tell can stall another
checks.rule: Every commit that changes what a session should hear sets tell-owed in its own transaction, tell() calls changed() on every registered session with allSettled, each bounded at 10 s, runs single-flight with one more pass, and clears tell-owed only after a pass with no rejection; rows: a changed() that never settles is bounded and later passes still run; one session rejecting leaves the others told and tell-owed set; a change committed during a pass is told by the extra pass; a commit whose tell never ran is told by the next alarm.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: tell every registered IMAP session of any change
FR-MAIL-034: without ever waiting for the telling
form 01a19daa event 8: a tell left in waitUntil may not arrive on deployed Cloudflare, so the owed tell is recovered
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A changed() that never settles, a lost waitUntil and a commit racing a pass exist only through a fake, never through a client.

checks.title: The alarm outlives a failing pull and finds what no ping announced
checks.rule: alarm() sets the next alarm 300 s on before it pulls while any session is registered, so a pull that throws leaves an alarm set, and the next alarm pulls a delivery no ping announced and tells it.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: tell every registered IMAP session of any change (a lost ping or a D1 outage would otherwise end the alarm chain after Cloudflare's six retries)
FR-MAIL-034: keep each mailbox in one Durable Object that pulls deliveries into SQLite
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A throwing D1 and a dropped ping are dependency failures a client cannot cause, so no scenario enters this path.

checks.title: A rebuilt mailbox reports a greater UIDVALIDITY
checks.rule: uid_validity is set once, when the tables are created, from the current time in seconds, so a mailbox object rebuilt after its SQLite is lost reports a greater value than the one before.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: assigning UIDs that only rise
rfc3501.2.3.1.1: a greater UIDVALIDITY whenever UIDs fail to persist
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Losing a Durable Object's storage is not something a client or Worker can do, so the rule is shown on a fresh object beside an old one.

checks.title: held returns expunged rows, more than 100 at a time
checks.rule: held(uids) returns the named rows in the order named, expunged or not, passing the UIDs as one JSON parameter, so 101 UIDs including expunged ones succeed under a SQLite wrapper that rejects more than 100 bound parameters.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: keeping an expunged message's row
form 01a19daa (seen failure): a held query broke every mailbox over 100 messages on waking
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The 100-parameter limit is a Durable Object SQLite limit that local runs do not enforce, so only a wrapper in a unit test shows it failing.

checks.title: An erased message keeps its row
checks.rule: Erasing an expunged message leaves its row: its UID is never reused, held still returns it so a woken session that names it is not closed with 1011, and a redelivery with the same Message-ID adds no UID.
proves: FR-MAIL-034: keeping an expunged message's row after its bytes are erased
toy 01a1a4ad (must hold, seen): removing the row closes a woken session with 1011; AUTOINCREMENT alone prevents UID reuse
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Erasure is driven by FR-MAIL-053's retention rule, not by a client, so this requirement's part of it is the row the erase must leave.

gaps.failure_way: A delivery commits more than ten minutes after its id, so the cursor has already passed it and it is never pulled
gaps.question: The SHALL says a late-committing delivery is never lost, and the form's cursor bounds lateness at ten minutes. Conflict between the SHALL and the form: is there a bound the receiver guarantees (and what makes it hold during a D1 or R2 outage), or must something sweep for deliveries behind the cursor?

gaps.failure_way: R2 or the parser fails transiently on a good message, which is written to skipped as unreadable and never read again
gaps.question: Is a transient read failure a bad message (skip for good, as the form says) or retried before it is skipped, and how many times? Skipping keeps later mail moving; retrying keeps this message. Either keeps every SHALL as written.

gaps.failure_way: A message with no Message-ID is delivered again by a provider's retry, before or after erasure
gaps.question: The form says a message with no Message-ID is always added; toy 01a1a4ad says the row must keep the blob key or such a message returns as a new UID. Does a redelivery of identical bytes with no Message-ID add a second UID or not?

gaps.failure_way: D1 is unavailable when a client selects, so the pull inside open throws
gaps.question: Does open answer with the rows already in SQLite and leave the pull to the alarm, or reject so the session closes with 1011? Both keep every SHALL true; the first keeps a client working through a D1 outage.
